# 12-Week Upper-Body Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 29-year-old female, recreational climber, right subacromial impingement (4 months physio), cleared for pain-free ROM only, no overhead loading.

## Guiding Principles

This programme is built around three priorities: protect the right shoulder by keeping all work below shoulder height for the first eight weeks, restore balanced scapular and rotator cuff function, and reintroduce loaded climbing-specific patterns (pull, hang, press) progressively. Every session begins with a shoulder prep circuit and ends with rotator cuff and thoracic mobility work. Rate of perceived exertion (RPE) caps progress through the phases — we stay submaximal until the shoulder proves it can handle load.

**Frequency:** 3 upper-body sessions per week (Mon/Wed/Fri suggested), with at least one full day between sessions. Lower body and conditioning slot in on alternate days at your discretion.

**Pain rule:** Any session-day pain above 3/10, or pain that lingers >24h, drops load 20% and revisits ROM. Sharp catching pain stops the exercise immediately.

---

## Phase 1 — Foundation & Scapular Control (Weeks 1–4)

Goal: rebuild scapular stability, posterior chain endurance, and grip without provoking the subacromial space. All pressing is horizontal or lower. Tempo is deliberate (3-1-1) to build control.

**Shoulder prep (every session, ~8 min):**
- Band pull-aparts 2×15
- Prone Y-T-W on bench 2×10 each, light DBs (1–2 kg)
- Serratus wall slides (below shoulder) 2×10
- Sleeper stretch + cross-body stretch, 2×30s each
- Banded ER at 0° abduction 2×15 each side

### Week 1 — Introduction, RPE 6

**Session A (Mon)**
1. Chest-supported DB row, 3×12, RPE 6
2. Half-kneeling landmine press (angle below shoulder), 3×10 each, RPE 6
3. Neutral-grip lat pulldown to chest (no full overhead), 3×12, RPE 6
4. Cable face pull (elbows below shoulder height), 3×15
5. Dead hang on jug — only if pain-free — 3×10s, otherwise scap pull-ups on bar 3×8
6. Farmer carry, 3×30m moderate

**Session B (Wed)**
1. Seated cable row, neutral grip, 3×12, RPE 6
2. Floor press DB, 3×10, RPE 6
3. Single-arm DB row (supported), 3×10 each
4. Prone trap-3 raise, 3×12 each, very light
5. Bottoms-up KB carry, 3×20m each
6. Pinch block hold, 3×20s

**Session C (Fri)**
1. Inverted row, feet on floor, 3×10, RPE 6
2. Push-up to TRX (hands below shoulder), 3×10
3. Half-kneeling cable row, 3×12 each
4. Side-lying DB ER, 3×12 each, light
5. Hangboard — 20mm edge, two-arm half-bodyweight assisted hangs, 4×10s
6. Dead bug, 3×10

### Week 2 — Same template, add 1 rep per set, RPE 6–7
### Week 3 — Add a top set: on lift #1 of each session, add a 4th set at RPE 7
### Week 4 — Deload: 2 sets only, RPE 5–6, keep all movements, focus on tempo

**Phase 1 reassessment:** pain-free horizontal pressing at 70% bodyweight load equivalent? Pain-free hanging? If yes, proceed.

---

## Phase 2 — Loading & Capacity (Weeks 5–8)

Goal: build strength in horizontal and pulling patterns, introduce light bodyweight hangs and pull progressions, begin loading the rotator cuff with intent. Still no overhead loading.

**Shoulder prep:** as Phase 1, but add prone scapular CARs and add resistance to ER/IR work.

### Week 5 — RPE 7

**Session A**
1. Barbell bench press, narrow grip, pause at chest, 4×6, RPE 7
2. Chest-supported row, 4×8
3. Landmine press (45° angle, still below face), 3×8 each, RPE 7
4. Lat pulldown, neutral grip, full ROM but stop short of full overhead lockout, 4×8
5. Half-bodyweight two-arm hang, 4×15s
6. Cable face pull + ER combo, 3×12

**Session B**
1. Single-arm DB row, 4×8 each, RPE 7
2. DB floor press, 4×8
3. Cable row, wide-grip to sternum, 3×10
4. Side-lying ER, moderate load, 3×10 each
5. Prone trap-3, 3×10 each
6. KB suitcase carry, 3×30m each

**Session C**
1. Inverted row, feet elevated, 4×8
2. Push-up, full ROM, hands shoulder-width, 4×AMRAP-2
3. Half-kneeling single-arm cable row, 3×10 each
4. Hangboard — 20mm edge, full bodyweight hang, 4×10s (RIGHT SHOULDER MONITORED)
5. Pallof press, 3×12 each
6. Pinch block, 3×25s

### Week 6 — add load, RPE 7–8
### Week 7 — peak loading, RPE 8 on main lifts, introduce one-arm hang assist (toe down) for 3×5s
### Week 8 — Deload: 60% loads, 3 sets, RPE 6

**Phase 2 reassessment:** bench press at bodyweight pain-free? One-arm assisted hang on right pain-free? If both yes, proceed to Phase 3 with overhead progression.

---

## Phase 3 — Climbing-Specific & Cautious Overhead Reintroduction (Weeks 9–12)

Goal: reintroduce overhead pulling and pressing if cleared, build pull-up capacity, integrate climbing-relevant grip and lock-off work. This phase assumes Phase 2 went well; if not, repeat Phase 2 week 7.

**Before week 9 begins, do an overhead screen:** pain-free full active flexion, pain-free Hawkins-Kennedy, pain-free empty can. All three clean = green light for overhead progression. Any one positive = continue Phase 2 template another 2 weeks.

### Week 9 — RPE 7

**Session A — Vertical pull focus**
1. Lat pulldown, full ROM including overhead start, 4×8, RPE 7
2. Bench press, 4×6, RPE 7
3. Assisted pull-up (band or machine), 3×6, controlled eccentric
4. Chest-supported row, 3×10
5. Hangboard — two-arm 20mm, 5×10s, full bodyweight
6. ER/IR cable work, 3×12 each

**Session B — Horizontal & accessory**
1. Single-arm DB row, 4×8, RPE 7–8
2. Landmine press, now to full overhead lockout on left, half-range on right, 3×8 each
3. Cable row, 3×10
4. Pallof press + iso hold, 3×30s each
5. Push-up variations 3×10
6. Hangboard — half-crimp, half bodyweight, 4×10s

**Session C — Pull-up build**
1. Negative pull-ups (3s eccentric), 4×4
2. Inverted row, feet elevated, 4×8
3. Seated DB press, neutral grip, light, ROM to where pain-free (likely 120–140°), 3×8 each
4. Face pull, 3×15
5. One-arm hang on left, assisted on right, 4×8s
6. Farmer carry, 3×40m heavy

### Week 10 — RPE 7–8, increase pull-up volume

Replace assisted pull-ups (Session A) with strict pull-ups 4×3 if able; otherwise 4×4 assisted with less assistance. Seated DB press progresses to slight incline if shoulder tolerates. Add lock-off holds at 90° and 120° on pull-up bar, 3×5s each.

### Week 11 — Peak, RPE 8

Test session at end of week 11:
- 3RM bench press
- Max strict pull-ups (or longest assisted hold)
- Max two-arm hangboard hang
- Pain-free overhead ROM check

Train-around-test: lighter Session B, full Session C.

### Week 12 — Deload & climb back in

Reduce gym volume to 2 sessions of 60% loads, 3 sets, RPE 6. Reintroduce easy climbing — slabs and vertical terrain only, no steep/overhead routes, no campusing, no dynos. Two short climbing sessions, with shoulder prep beforehand.

---

## Recovery & Adjuncts Across All Phases

- **Sleep:** 7–9 h, non-negotiable for rotator cuff tissue remodelling.
- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight, prioritised across 3–4 meals.
- **Daily mobility (5 min):** thoracic extension on foam roller, doorway pec stretch (low arm position only in Phase 1), sleeper stretch.
- **Weekly contact with physio** in Phase 1 and 2, monthly in Phase 3.
- **Climbing:** none in Phases 1–2 except very light slab traversing if physio agrees. Reintroduce in Week 12 only.

## Red Flags to Pause Programme

- Night pain returning
- Painful arc 60–120° reappearing
- Loss of active ROM week-on-week
- Pain that persists beyond session day

Any of these — back to physio before next session.

Let me know your client's training history, current bench/row numbers, and hangboard baseline if you have them, and I'll tighten the starting loads.

# Nutrition Plan — Body Recomposition

Recomposition (simultaneous fat loss and muscle gain) works best for clients who are training hard, undertrained relative to their potential, and not in a large deficit. Your client fits the brief: she's coming back from injury, will be progressively loading new tissue, and is a recreational climber rather than a heavily trained athlete. A small calorie deficit with high protein and well-timed carbohydrates around training should drive the result over 12 weeks.

I need a few numbers to make this exact, so I've built the plan around assumed values you can swap out. **Assumed:** 29F, 65 kg, ~165 cm, moderately active (climbing + 3 gym sessions). Adjust proportionally if her stats differ.

---

## Calorie & Macro Target

**Estimated maintenance:** ~2,150 kcal/day
**Recomp target:** ~1,950 kcal/day (≈10% deficit)

| Macro | Grams/day | kcal | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protein | 130 g (2.0 g/kg) | 520 | 27% |
| Fat | 65 g (1.0 g/kg) | 585 | 30% |
| Carbohydrate | 210 g | 840 | 43% |

Protein is the non-negotiable lever for recomposition — high enough to drive muscle protein synthesis while in a deficit, and to protect lean mass. Carbs are kept moderate-to-high to support strength training and climbing performance. Fat sits at the floor of what's needed for hormonal health (don't drop below 0.8 g/kg).

**Adjustment rule:** if bodyweight is stable or trending down 0.2–0.4 kg/week and strength is climbing, you're on target. If she's losing >0.5 kg/week, add 150 kcal (mostly carbs). If no change after 3 weeks, drop 100 kcal.

---

## Meal Structure & Timing

Four meals per day, with protein anchored at ≥30 g per meal to maximise leucine threshold and muscle protein synthesis per feeding. Carbs are loaded around training.

### Training day template (~1,950 kcal)

**Breakfast (~450 kcal):** 35 g protein, 50 g carb, 12 g fat
- Greek yoghurt (200 g, 0% fat) + 40 g oats + 100 g berries + 15 g almonds + scoop whey if needed to hit protein

**Pre-training snack, 60–90 min out (~300 kcal):** 25 g protein, 40 g carb, 5 g fat
- 2 eggs + 1 slice wholegrain toast + banana
- *or* protein shake + rice cakes with honey

**Post-training/lunch, within 90 min (~600 kcal):** 40 g protein, 70 g carb, 15 g fat
- 130 g chicken or tofu + 80 g (dry) rice or quinoa + large mixed veg + 1 tbsp olive oil

**Dinner (~600 kcal):** 35 g protein, 50 g carb, 25 g fat
- 150 g salmon/white fish/lean beef + roast potatoes (250 g) + greens + olive oil/avocado

### Rest day template (~1,800 kcal)
Drop carbs by ~50 g (smaller portions of rice/oats), keep protein and fat the same. This creates a natural carb cycle: higher on training days for performance, lower on rest days for slightly bigger deficit.

---

## Recovery & Injury-Specific Nutrition

The shoulder is still remodelling. A few additions matter more here than they would for a healthy client:

- **Collagen + vitamin C, 60 min pre-training:** 15 g hydrolysed collagen + 50 mg vitamin C (or eat with kiwi/orange). Evidence is modest but the upside is real for tendon and capsular tissue, and there's no downside.
- **Omega-3:** 2 g EPA+DHA daily. Anti-inflammatory effect and supports tendon healing.
- **Vitamin D:** test levels; supplement to 1000–2000 IU/day if below 75 nmol/L. Low D is common in indoor athletes and impairs muscle recovery.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 5 g/day. Recomposition-friendly, well-evidenced for strength gains, no contraindication with her presentation.

---

## Protein Sources (per 30 g protein serving)

- 120 g cooked chicken breast
- 130 g cooked white fish
- 110 g cooked lean beef
- 170 g Greek yoghurt + 1 scoop whey
- 5 large eggs (or 3 eggs + 50 g cheese)
- 200 g firm tofu + 30 g pumpkin seeds
- 1 scoop whey (25 g) + 200 ml milk

---

## Hydration & Climbing-Specific Notes

- **Fluid:** 2.5–3 L/day, more on climbing days. Climbing in a chalk-and-friction-dependent sport rewards being well-hydrated but not over-watered — clear-pale urine is the target.
- **Caffeine:** up to 3 mg/kg (≈200 mg) pre-training is fine and helpful. Avoid >4 mg/kg if she trains evenings, sleep matters more here than the ergogenic effect.
- **Alcohol:** the honest conversation. >2 standard drinks impairs muscle protein synthesis for ~24 h and disrupts sleep, which is where her shoulder tissue actually heals. Suggest ≤3 drinks per week, ideally not on training nights.

---

## Phase-Specific Adjustments

Recomposition isn't linear over 12 weeks. Match nutrition to the training phase:

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) — Foundation:** Stick to 1,950 kcal training days / 1,800 rest. Training volume is moderate, so the deficit is comfortable. Weigh weekly, same time, same conditions.

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) — Loading:** Add 100 kcal on training days (mostly post-training carbs — extra 25 g rice/potato). Training stress is higher, recovery demand goes up. Maintain rest-day kcal.

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) — Specific & Test:** Bring training-day intake back to maintenance (≈2,150 kcal) for the test week (Week 11) — you want her fuelled to express strength, not in a deficit. Return to deficit Week 12 if she wants to keep the trajectory beyond the programme.

---

## Tracking & Markers

Don't rely on the scale alone — recomposition is invisible to bodyweight. Track:

1. **Bodyweight:** weekly average (5 morning weigh-ins), not single readings

# Cardio Programme — 2×/Week, Climbing-Day Endurance Focus

Long climbing days are a hybrid demand: 6–10 hours of low-intensity aerobic work (approach, belaying, route-finding) punctuated by high-intensity anaerobic bursts (hard sequences, cruxes), with the ability to recover between pitches being the rate-limiter. The cardio plan trains both ends: a Zone 2 base session for aerobic capacity and recovery between efforts, and a higher-intensity session for the anaerobic ceiling and lactate clearance.

**Scheduling:** Slot cardio on Tue and Sat — between upper-body sessions and not back-to-back. Keep at least 6 hours between gym and cardio if same day.

**Modality choice:** Avoid running-heavy weeks initially (joint load + shoulder posture under fatigue). Prioritise modalities that don't aggravate the shoulder:
- **Best:** stationary bike, assault bike (lower body only), incline treadmill walk, stair climber, hiking, rowing erg (only if pain-free — test in Phase 2)
- **Good:** outdoor cycling, trail walking with light pack
- **Avoid in Phases 1–2:** rowing erg, swimming, anything with repetitive overhead or end-range shoulder loading

**Heart rate zones (estimate, 220−age = 191 max):**
- Zone 2: 115–133 bpm (60–70% max) — conversational, nasal breathing possible
- Zone 3: 134–152 bpm — comfortably hard, sentences only
- Zone 4: 153–172 bpm — hard, single words
- Zone 5: 173+ bpm — maximal

Use a chest strap or radial pulse check; RPE works fine if no monitor.

## Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) — Aerobic Base

Goal: build mitochondrial density and capillarisation, raise the floor of aerobic capacity, get her comfortable accumulating training volume without aggravating the shoulder. Both sessions are Zone 2 — boring on purpose.

### Session 1 (Tue) — Steady Zone 2
- Week 1: 30 min stationary bike or incline walk @ Zone 2
- Week 2: 35 min
- Week 3: 40 min
- Week 4 (deload): 30 min

### Session 2 (Sat) — Long Zone 2
- Week 1: 45 min — outdoor walk/hike, easy cycle, or mixed
- Week 2: 50 min
- Week 3: 60 min — ideally on hilly terrain to mimic approach demand
- Week 4 (deload): 45 min

**Cue:** if she can't hold a conversation, she's too high. Heart rate drift is normal — keep effort steady even if HR creeps up in the last third.

## Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) — Add Intensity Ceiling

Goal: keep building base, introduce intervals to lift VO₂max and lactate threshold. This is where between-pitch recovery actually improves.

### Session 1 (Tue) — Intervals

**Week 5 — VO₂ intervals**
Warm-up 10 min easy → 5 × (2 min Zone 4 / 2 min Zone 1) → 5 min cooldown. Total ~30 min.

**Week 6 — Threshold intervals**
Warm-up 10 min → 4 × (4 min Zone 3–low 4 / 2 min Zone 1) → 5 min cooldown. Total ~40 min.

**Week 7 — VO₂ progression**
Warm-up 10 min → 6 × (2 min Zone 4 / 2 min Zone 1) → 5 min cooldown. Total ~35 min.

**Week 8 (deload)**
Warm-up 10 min → 3 × (3 min Zone 3 / 3 min Zone 1) → 5 min cooldown. Total ~30 min.

Modality for intervals: stationary bike is ideal — no impact, no shoulder load, easy to dial intensity precisely. Incline treadmill at fast walk/light jog works if she prefers.

### Session 2 (Sat) — Long Zone 2 with terrain
- Week 5: 60 min hilly walk/hike or cycle
- Week 6: 70 min
- Week 7: 75 min, add a light daypack (4–5 kg) if hiking
- Week 8 (deload): 50 min

The Saturday session is now explicitly an **approach simulation**. Hills, mixed terrain, light pack. This is the most climbing-specific aerobic work she'll do.

## Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) — Specificity & Climbing Reintroduction

Goal: bridge to actual climbing-day demand. Mix intensities, add a packed hike, taper into Week 12 so she's fresh for climbing reintroduction.

### Session 1 (Tue) — Mixed intervals or climbing-specific circuit

**Week 9 — Lactate clearance intervals**
Warm-up 10 min → 8 × (90s Zone 4 / 90s Zone 2 *active* recovery, not Zone 1) → 5 min cooldown. The active recovery trains lactate clearance — the same physiological skill as recovering on a no-hands rest mid-route. Total ~35 min.

**Week 10 — Pyramid**
Warm-up 10 min → 1/2/3/2/1 min Zone 4 with equal Zone 1 between → 5 min cooldown. Total ~30 min.

**Week 11 (test week) — Easy aerobic only**
40 min steady Zone 2. Don't dig into reserves before strength testing.

**Week 12 — Climbing-day rehearsal**

- Week 10: 2 h with 6–7 kg pack — closest thing to a real approach

# Hangboard & Climbing-Specific Prep — Phase 2 Onward

The strength plan already includes light hangboard work as accessory; this expands it into a proper progression toward long climbing days. The principle: rebuild contact strength and finger-tendon capacity *slowly* — fingers adapt over months, not weeks, and her shoulder is the limiter on hanging load until at least Phase 3.

**Two non-negotiables:**
1. Hangboard work happens **fresh**, before strength training, not after. Tired fingers + compromised shoulder = injury.
2. Right shoulder dictates load on all hanging work. If left could hang harder, left waits.

**Equipment assumed:** standard hangboard (Beastmaker 1000, Tension Grindstone, or similar) with 20 mm edge, jugs, and a pulley/band system for assisted hangs. Lattice or Tindeq for measured pulls is ideal but not required.

---

## Phase 2 Hangboard Integration (Weeks 5–8)

This is a re-introduction block, not a strength block. Volume is low, holds are friendly (open-hand or half-crimp on 20 mm), and the goal is tissue tolerance — finger pulleys, A2/A4, and shoulder capsule all need to re-learn the load.

**Placement:** start of Session A and Session C (the two sessions that already include hangboard work in the strength plan). Replace the existing hangboard line with the progression below.

### Week 5 — Tissue prep
- 20 mm edge, half-crimp or open-hand (her choice — whichever is pain-free)
- 5 × 7s hang / 53s rest, two-arm, full bodyweight if pain-free on right; otherwise assist with pulley to 90% BW
- RPE 5–6, should feel easy
- Both sessions A and C

### Week 6 — Add volume
- Same hold, same edge
- 6 × 7s / 53s rest
- RPE 6
- Both sessions

### Week 7 — Introduce repeaters
- 20 mm half-crimp, two-arm
- 3 sets of 6 × (7s hang / 3s rest), 2 min between sets
- This is the classic "7/3 repeater" — the building block for endurance hangs
- RPE 6–7
- Session A only. Session C keeps the 6×7s max-hang style.

### Week 8 (deload)
- 4 × 7s / 53s rest, two-arm, RPE 5
- Session A only; drop hangboard from Session C
- Shoulder gets a break

**Check at end of Phase 2:** can she hang full bodyweight on 20 mm half-crimp for 10s without right-shoulder symptom? If yes → Phase 3 progressions. If no → repeat Week 7 for another two weeks before progressing.

Goal: build genuine contact strength, introduce one-arm work cautiously, layer in climbing-specific endurance, and finish ready for slab/vertical days. The shoulder is now the gating factor on overhead load — every hang is also a shoulder strengthening exercise.

- Bodyweight only
- RPE 7

- Stay off steep terrain
- Treat as skill + tissue exposure, not a workout
- Optional this week, encouraged

## Climbing-Specific Prep Routine

Before *every* climbing session in Phase 3, a 15-minute on-the-wall warm-up that doubles as shoulder prep. Same components, climbing-context delivery.

**1. General warm-up (3 min):** light cardio — bike, jumping jacks, or brisk walk to the crag/wall

**2. Shoulder prep (5 min):**
- Band pull-aparts × 15
- Banded ER at 0° × 15 each
- Scapular push-up × 10
- Sleeper stretch × 30s each
- Wall serratus slides × 10

**3. Finger warm-up (4 min):**
- Easy hangboard or first-route equivalent
- 3 × 10s hangs on a jug or 25 mm+ edge, very light
- Open-hand only — no crimping cold

**4. Movement warm-up (3 min):**
- 2 easy traverses or 1 easy route well below limit
- Focus on slow, deliberate movement; feel both shoulders engage symmetrically

**Total: ~15 min.** Don't skip this for at least the first 3 months back climbing.

## Holds, Grip Types & What to Avoid

**Use throughout Phase 2–3:**
- Open-hand
- Half-crimp on 20 mm
- Jugs

**Introduce cautiously in late Phase 3 (Week 11+):**
- Three-finger drag
- Pinches (already in strength plan)

**Avoid for the full 12 weeks:**
- Full crimp (closed) — high A2 pulley load, not worth the risk while she's rebuilding
- Slopers on the hangboard — high shoulder demand at end-range
- Pockets, especially monos and two-finger — disproportionate tendon load on tissue that hasn't trained for months
- Campus board — period.
- One-arm unassisted hangs — not until well past Week 12, and only after a proper one-arm progression with cleared shoulder

# Phase 3 Revision — Peaking for a Week 12 Climbing Trip

Peaking changes the structure of Phase 3 substantially. The original plan treated Week 12 as a *reintroduction*; now Week 12 is the **performance week**, which means we have to compress strength gains into Weeks 9–10, sharpen in Week 11, and taper into Week 12 so she arrives fresh, strong, and with the shoulder loaded enough times to be confident — but not beaten up.

**Critical caveat first:** pushing intensity on a shoulder 4 months post-impingement, only just cleared for overhead, carries real risk. The single biggest mistake would be loading the right shoulder hard in Weeks 9–10 to "catch up" before the trip. The shoulder gets honest progressive load; everything else — fingers, pull strength, climbing-specific endurance — is where we push.

Confirm with the trainer/client and ideally her physio before running this version. If overhead clearance is borderline at end of Week 8, run the original Phase 3 instead and accept the trip is a "feel it out" trip, not a performance trip.

**Assumptions for this revision:**
- Phase 2 end-screen was clean (pain-free overhead, Hawkins-Kennedy, empty can)
- Trip terrain is multi-pitch / long single-pitch trad or sport, not bouldering or steep sport — "long climbing days" implies endurance + moderate intensity, not max bouldering
- She has 12 weeks total; the trip is Week 12

# Mobility Programme

Mobility work for this client serves three jobs: keep the right shoulder progressing through pain-free ROM and protect the gains the physio made, address the postural and tissue restrictions that climbers universally accumulate (thoracic kyphosis, internally rotated shoulders, tight hip flexors, stiff wrists), and prepare tissue for the specific demands of each session. It is not generic stretching — it's targeted, dosed, and tracked.

**Three placements:**
1. **Pre-session mobility** — built into warm-ups (already in the strength and climbing plans)
2. **Daily mobility** — 10 min, every day, non-negotiable
3. **Long mobility session** — 30–40 min, 1× per week

---

## Daily Mobility (10 min, every day)

Same routine every day so it becomes automatic. Done in the morning, or before bed — whichever sticks. The shoulder work here is the floor: even on a total rest day, this happens.

### The 10-minute sequence

**1. Cat-cow + thread the needle (90s)**
- 5 cat-cow on all fours, slow
- Thread the needle each side, 30s hold
- Wakes up thoracic rotation, which is the climber's most consistently restricted segment

**2. World's greatest stretch (90s)**
- Each side: lunge, hand to floor inside front foot, opposite hand reaches up with thoracic rotation
- 3 reps each side, 5s hold at top
- Hits hip flexor, adductor, thoracic, shoulder — all in one

**3. Doorway pec stretch (60s)**
- Arm at 90° (NOT overhead — keep at or below shoulder height through Phases 1–2; overhead doorway stretch can be added Week 9 if pain-free)
- 30s each side
- Targets pec minor — the muscle most responsible for pulling the scapula forward and contributing to subacromial narrowing

**4. Sleeper stretch (60s)**
- Side-lying, shoulder at 90°, elbow at 90°, gently rotate forearm toward floor
- 30s each side
- Posterior capsule mobility — directly relevant to impingement; this is the single most important stretch for her

**5. Thoracic extension on foam roller (90s)**
- Roller across mid-back, hands behind head, extend over roller
- 4–5 positions from low thoracic to high thoracic
- 5 breaths at each position
- Opens up the segments that have to extend for any overhead movement

**6. Wrist + forearm prep (90s)**
- Wrist flexor stretch: palm up, pull fingers back, 30s each side
- Wrist extensor stretch: palm down, pull fingers down, 30s each side
- Wrist CARs: 5 controlled circles each direction
- Climbers under-train this and pay for it; especially relevant once hangboard intensifies

**7. Hip flexor stretch — couch stretch or kneeling (90s)**
- 45s each side
- Tight hip flexors steal lumbar extension and force the thoracic spine to compensate, which then steals shoulder mobility — chain effect

**8. Shoulder CARs (60s)**
- Controlled articular rotations, both shoulders, 3 each direction
- Slow, deliberate, full range that is *pain-free* on the right (range will be smaller than left initially — that's fine, don't force symmetry)
- This is also a daily diagnostic: she'll feel which days the shoulder is tighter

**Total: ~10 min.** Time it once or twice, then run it from memory.

## Long Mobility Session (30–40 min, 1× per week)

Placed on Sunday or Thursday — whichever is the lower-load day. This is the session where she addresses restrictions that the daily 10 min can't unwind. Treat it like a training session in the calendar.

### Structure

**1. General warm-up (5 min)**
- Easy bike or walk, then a full body movement flow: cat-cow → child's pose → downward dog → low lunge each side → standing forward fold → standing roll-up

**2. Thoracic spine block (8 min)**
The single most important region for a climber with shoulder history.

- Foam roller thoracic extensions: 4 positions, 5 breaths each
- Open book stretch (side-lying thoracic rotation): 8 reps each side, slow, 2s hold at end range
- Quadruped thoracic rotation, hand behind head: 8 each side
- Wall thoracic extension (hands on wall, hips back, chest sinks): 8 reps with 2s hold

**3. Shoulder block (10 min)**

- Sleeper stretch: 2 × 45s each
- Cross-body stretch: 2 × 30s each
- Banded shoulder distraction (band overhead, lean back) — *only if cleared for overhead*, so Week 9+: 2 × 30s each
- PNC shoulder mobility on table or floor — internal and external rotation at 90°, 8 slow reps each direction
- Wall slides (slow, with breath): 2 × 8
- Pec minor smash with lacrosse ball or massage ball, against wall: 60s each side

**4. Hip block (8 min)**
Climbers neglect this and it costs them. Tight hips force compensation up the chain.

- Couch stretch: 90s each side
- 90/90 hip switches: 10 reps slow
- Pigeon: 90s each side
- Adductor rock-backs: 10 reps slow
- Frog stretch: 60s

**5. Forearm and wrist block (5 min)**
Critical given the hangboard volume coming in Phases 2–3.

- Forearm smash with ball or pin-and-stretch through full wrist ROM: 90s each forearm
- Prayer stretch (palms together, lower hands): 45s
- Reverse prayer stretch (backs of hands together): 45s
- Wrist push-up holds, light: 3 × 15s

**6. Decompression / breathing (4 min)**
End with parasympathetic downregulation — useful for recovery, sleep, and tissue remodelling.

- Legs up the wall: 3 min
- 4-7-8 breathing (inhale 4s, hold 7s, exhale 8s): 4 rounds

## Phase-Specific Mobility Adjustments

### Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4)
- All shoulder work below shoulder height
- No banded overhead distractions
- Pec stretches with arm at 60–80°, never above shoulder
- Daily routine emphasis: sleeper stretch and posterior capsule work — these directly target the impingement mechanism
- Long session keeps the overhead-restricted version of shoulder block

### Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8)
- Begin testing pain-free range above shoulder height in CARs only — never under load
- Add scapular wall slides with arms higher each week if pain-free
- Pec minor stretching can progress arm position higher if pain-free
- Long session: add wall angels (slow, full ROM that is pain-free)

### Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) — Peaking
- Overhead work cleared (assuming Phase 2 end-screen was clean)
- Add banded shoulder distractions to daily routine
- Add active overhead reach progressions: wall slide → kettlebell armbar (light) → Turkish get-up to elbow only
- **Week 11–12:** drop intensity of mobility work along with strength taper. Daily routine continues; long session shortens to 20 min and is fully restorative — no end-range pushing, no PNF, just maintenance and decompression. Going into a trip with freshly mobilised tissue can leave joints feeling unstable — last week is *maintenance only*.

## Trip-Specific Mobility (Week 12, on trip)

Climbing trips are when mobility most often gets dropped — usually exactly when it matters most. Cumulative fatigue, sleeping on different surfaces, long days, and travel all stiffen the system.

**Every morning of the trip (8 min):**
- World's greatest stretch (90s)
- Sleeper stretch (60s each)
- Doorway pec stretch (60s each)
- Thoracic extension over rolled towel or pack if no roller (60s)
- Hip flexor stretch (60s each)
- Shoulder CARs (60s)

**Every evening (5 min):**
- Forearm smash (any ball, or against a rock if needed) (60s each)
- Sleeper stretch (45s each)
- Legs up the wall against tent/van/hotel wall (3 min)

This is the minimum effective dose to keep her moving well across consecutive climbing days. If she does only this on trip, she'll start Day 4 feeling like Day 2.

## Specific Restrictions to Watch

Based on her presentation, three things are highly likely to show up and worth tracking:

**1. Posterior capsule tightness (right shoulder)**
- Test: lying on right side, shoulder/elbow at 90°, how far does the forearm drop toward the floor before she feels block or pain? Compare to left.
- Recheck every 2 weeks
- Goal: within 10° of left side by Week 8, symmetrical by Week 12
- This is the most direct contributor to impingement; sleeper stretch is the primary tool

**2. Pec minor tightness (both sides, worse on right)**
- Test: lying supine, arms by sides, does the back of the shoulder rest flat against the floor? On the affected side it often hovers.
- Recheck every 2 weeks
- Goal: both shoulders flat to floor by Week 8

**3. Thoracic extension restriction**
- Test: seated against a wall, arms overhead with thumbs pointing back. Can she touch thumbs to wall without arching the lower back? Most climbers can't initially.
- Recheck every 4 weeks
- Goal: thumbs to wall, lumbar flat, by Week 12

## What Mobility Work Does NOT Include

A few things to actively avoid given her presentation:

- **Aggressive end-range overhead stretching in Phases 1–2** — the impingement mechanism is end-range under load; we don't reproduce it under stretch either
- **Static stretching immediately before strength sessions** — keep pre-session work dynamic and activating; save long holds for daily routine and long session
- **PNF stretching on the right shoulder** — too aggressive for tissue still in rehabilitation; revisit Week 9+ only if cleared
- **Cracking/manipulation of the thoracic spine by anyone other than her physio** — leave that to professionals who know her case
- **Foam rolling directly on the front of the shoulder or under the clavicle** — risk of compressing the neurovascular structures and the inflamed tissue itself

## Tracking

Three data points, recorded weekly:

1. **Posterior capsule test** (sleeper stretch position, degrees from floor) — both sides
2. **Active shoulder flexion** — back against wall, arm overhead, how high before lumbar arches or shoulder hitches?
3. **Subjective stiffness on waking** — 0–10, right shoulder specifically

A 0.5/10 reduction in waking stiffness across 4 weeks is meaningful. A return to baseline tightness for 3+ days running means session loads are slightly too high, regardless of in-session pain.

# Saturday Finisher Day

This needs to slot in without disrupting recovery for the rest of the programme. The current Saturday slot has the long Zone 2 cardio session — a packed hike or long bike. That's not negotiable in Phase 3 because it's training the exact aerobic system her trip demands.

**Solution:** the finisher *is* the Saturday cardio session, restructured. **Hard rules for this session:**
- Always full warm-up first (shoulder prep + general warm-up, 12 min)
- Cap intensity at RPE 8 — this is *fun hard*, not *grind hard*
- No overhead loading in Phases 1–2 (same rule as everywhere else)

| 3 Wk 12 | Trip / rest | Trip |

Z2: 115–133 · Z3: 134–152 · Z4: 153–172 · Z5: 173+

---

## Hangboard Progression

| Phase / Wk | Protocol | Hold | Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wk 1–4 | Easy hangs, scap pull-ups | Jugs, 20 mm | Half-BW assisted |
| Wk 5 | 5×7s/53s | 20 mm half-crimp | BW or 90% assisted |
| Wk 6 | 6×7s/53s | 20 mm | BW |
| Wk 7 | 3 × 6 × (7s/3s) repeaters + 6×7s | 20 mm | BW |
| Wk 8 | 4×7s, very light | 20 mm | BW, RPE 5 |
| Wk 9 | 5×10s max + 4 × 6 × (7s/3s) | 20 mm | +2–5 kg if able |
| Wk 10 | **Peak:** 4×8s max + assisted 1-arm 4×6s | 20 mm | Max loadable |
| Wk 11 | Single 10s max test + 3×5s 1-arm test | 20 mm | Benchmark |
| Wk 12 | 4×7s maintenance Mon only | 20 mm | 50% max |

**Avoid throughout:** full crimp, slopers, pockets, monos, campus, one-arm unassisted hangs.

---

## Saturday Finisher Day

Replaces (or folds in) Saturday cardio. Full-body, fun, climbing-relevant.

**Phase 1:** Warm-up + 25 min Z2 hike + playground circuit + carry finisher
**Phase 2:** Warm-up + hill repeats + EMOM + strongman block
**Phase 3 Wk 9:** Pack hike + "crag day" circuit + carry medley
**Phase 3 Wk 10:** 2h pack hike, no circuit
**Phase 3 Wk 11:** Easy Z2 + fun power moves, low volume

Cap: 75 min. RPE 8 ceiling. No overhead, no max fingers, no shoulder-fatiguing burpees.

---

## Mobility

**Daily (10 min):** cat-cow + thread the needle, world's greatest stretch, doorway pec (below shoulder P1–2), sleeper stretch, thoracic foam roller, wrist/forearm, hip flexor, shoulder CARs.

**Pre-session:** built into every warm-up (8 min strength prep, 15 min climbing prep, 3 min cardio prep).

**Long session (Thu, 30–40 min):** thoracic block, shoulder block, hip block, forearm block, breathing.

**Tracking:** posterior capsule test, active shoulder flexion, waking stiffness.

---

## Nutrition

**Target:** ~1,950 kcal training days / ~1,800 rest, recomposition deficit.

**Macros:** 130 g protein (2.0 g/kg) · 65 g fat (1.0 g/kg) · 210 g carbs

**Phase shifts:**
- Phase 1: 1,950 / 1,800
- Phase 2: 2,050 training / 1,800 rest (more carbs around training)
- Phase 3 Wk 11: maintenance 2,150 across the week (top up glycogen)
- Phase 3 Wk 12 trip: maintenance + intra-day fuelling

**Supplements:** 15 g collagen + 50 mg vit C pre-training, 2 g omega-3 daily, vit D if low, 5 g creatine.

**Tracking:** weekly bodyweight average, waist circumference, photos every 4 weeks, strength markers should increase.

---

## Key Tests and Benchmarks

| When | Test |
|---|---|
| Wk 1 | Baselines: shoulder ROM, posterior capsule, pec minor, thoracic ext, current strength markers |
| End Wk 4 | Phase 1 reassessment: pain-free horizontal press at ~70% BW load? Pain-free hanging? |
| End Wk 8 | Phase 2 shoulder screen: pain-free Hawkins-Kennedy, empty can, full active flexion. **All three must be clean to enter overhead progression.** |
| End Wk 10 | Peak load check: shoulder ≤3/10 next day, no night pain, pull strength up vs Phase 2 — **gate for proceeding to peaking vs deload-to-trip** |
| Wk 11 | Performance tests: bench 3RM, max strict pull-ups, two-arm max hang on 20 mm, one-arm assist required |
| Wk 12 | Trip = the real-world test |

---

## Red Flags — Programme-Wide

**Pause and reassess:**
- Pain >3/10 in session, or lingering >24h
- Night pain returning
- Painful arc 60–120° reappearing
- Loss of active ROM week-on-week
- Resting HR up >7 bpm for 3+ days
- Persistent sleep disturbance

**Stop immediately, contact physio:**
- Sharp catching pain during pulls or hangs
- Pulley pop/click/sharp finger pain
- Numbness or tingling down right arm
- Loss of >15° active flexion vs Week 8 baseline

**Trip-cancellation criteria (have this conversation early in Phase 3):**
- Night pain + ROM loss going into Week 10
- Failed Week 10 peak check with shoulder symptoms
- Two consecutive sessions where shoulder limits pulling

---

## Information Still Needed to Lock Loads

To turn this from a template into prescribed loads:

1. Current bodyweight and height
2. Current bench, row, and pull-up numbers (or assisted variants)
3. Pre-injury hangboard baseline if known (20 mm max-hang weight)
4. Trip details: exact dates, terrain (sport / trad / multi-pitch / alpine), expected grade range, day length
5. Resting HR and any cardio baseline (5K time, FTP, or current approach pace)
6. Phase 2 end-screen results (cleared for overhead?)
7. Equipment access on Saturdays (full gym, home, outdoor only)
8. Food preferences, intolerances, cooking time available
9. Physio's current restrictions and which exercises she's been doing in rehab — so we can integrate, not parallel
10. Posterior capsule, pec minor, and thoracic extension baselines (or take them in session 1)

# Full 12-Week Programme Summary

**Client:** 29F, recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, 4 months physio, cleared for pain-free ROM, no overhead loading at start. **Goal:** peak for a long climbing day trip in Week 12.

---

## Programme Architecture

| Element | Frequency | Notes |
|---|---|---|

## Phase Overview

### Phase 1 — Foundation & Scapular Control (Weeks 1–4)
Rebuild scapular control, posterior chain endurance, grip. All work below shoulder height. Tempo controlled. RPE 6, building to RPE 6–7. Week 4 deload.

### Phase 2 — Loading & Capacity (Weeks 5–8)
Build horizontal strength, introduce hangboard repeaters, light bodyweight hangs. Still no overhead. RPE 7–8 on main lifts. Week 8 deload. End-of-phase shoulder screen.

### Phase 3 — Peaking for Climbing Trip (Weeks 9–12)
**Revised for trip peaking.** Intensification (Wk 9), peak load (Wk 10), sharpening (Wk 11), trip (Wk 12). Cautious overhead reintroduction. Hangboard peaks Wk 10. Climbing volume builds Wk 9–10, tapers Wk 11–12.

## Red Flags — Programme-Wide

**Pause and reassess:**
- Pain >3/10 in session, or lingering >24h
- Night pain returning
- Painful arc 60–120° reappearing
- Loss of active ROM week-on-week
- Resting HR up >7 bpm for 3+ days
- Persistent sleep disturbance

**Stop immediately, contact physio:**
- Sharp catching pain during pulls or hangs
- Pulley pop/click/sharp finger pain
- Numbness or tingling down right arm
- Loss of >15° active flexion vs Week 8 baseline

**Trip-cancellation criteria (have this conversation early in Phase 3):**
- Night pain + ROM loss going into Week 10
- Failed Week 10 peak check with shoulder symptoms
- Two consecutive sessions where shoulder limits pulling
